title: Template Method

act2.summary: a fourth instrument that must SKIP the calibrate step entirely, not run it as a no-op

solutions.title: A shared pipeline function taking instrument hooks
solutions.tradeoff: A new instrument that fits the five fixed steps is one new file. A new instrument that needs to skip one of the five steps is not: it means reopening the shared pipeline and the hooks interface, which is exactly the file the pattern exists to stop you from reopening.

reviewFocus: Is there still exactly one place that knows the order of the five steps, after the guide camera was added?
Did making calibrate optional quietly make it meaningless to skip for the wrong reason in a future instrument (a lazy implementer just omitting it)?
Is the walkthrough honest that this route did NOT clearly win against the no-pattern baseline - fewer files but fewer hunks on one side, more total lines on the other?
Would a stage-list design (each instrument declares an ordered array of named steps) have been a better bet from the start, given this axis was foreseeable?
Does the git log show the skeleton being extracted before the instruments were split into files, or the other way around?
